answer: A ventilation engineer treats each agent’s identity like a lantern check at the shaft collar, requiring a continuously measured airflow signature tied to a unique underground sensor before any agent gains network standing. Each identity must solve a cipher keyed to that sensor’s live readings, so forging one costs the attacker real sensor hardware plus sustained physical access to keep readings current. This garden of verified nodes still fails if hardware is stolen wholesale, capping resistance at the price of compromise rather than eliminating it.
